semantic_distinctions.title: C vs CUDA C/C++
semantic_distinctions.description: C/C++ is the language base; CUDA adds GPU execution, memory and API extensions.

semantic_distinctions.title: Host vs device
semantic_distinctions.description: Host code runs on CPU; device kernels run on GPU.

semantic_distinctions.title: Runtime API vs Driver API
semantic_distinctions.description: Runtime is higher-level/single-source; Driver API is lower-level/non-single-source.

semantic_distinctions.title: Grid vs block vs thread
semantic_distinctions.description: Grid contains blocks; blocks contain threads; warps group 32 threads.

semantic_distinctions.title: Shared vs global memory
semantic_distinctions.description: Shared memory is block-shared/user-managed; global memory is device-wide.

semantic_distinctions.title: PTX vs SASS
semantic_distinctions.description: PTX is intermediate representation; SASS is hardware machine instruction representation.

semantic_distinctions.title: CUDA vs ROCm
semantic_distinctions.description: CUDA is proprietary NVIDIA software; ROCm is open-source AMD software.

semantic_distinctions.title: CUDA vs oneAPI
semantic_distinctions.description: CUDA is NVIDIA-specific; oneAPI targets multiple architectures through open specifications.

semantic_distinctions.title: Uniform vs divergent warp control flow
semantic_distinctions.description: Uniform branches preserve SIMD efficiency; divergence reduces it.

semantic_distinctions.title: Computation vs transfer cost
semantic_distinctions.description: Host/device transfers can limit end-to-end acceleration.

misconceptions.correction: CUDA C/C++ adds GPU kernels, execution hierarchy, memory APIs and a CUDA compilation/runtime model.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA runs all code on the GPU
misconceptions.correction: Host code remains CPU-side while kernels execute on the GPU.

misconceptions.claim: A block is a GPU core
misconceptions.correction: A block is a logical group of threads scheduled onto streaming multiprocessors.

misconceptions.claim: A thread is a CUDA core
misconceptions.correction: Threads are logical execution contexts; hardware execution is organized through warps and SMs.
PTX is an intermediate representation that is lowered toward GPU machine instructions.
Warp divergence, memory movement, architecture and occupancy constraints can dominate.
Shared memory is a distinct fast user-managed region shared by block threads.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA runs natively on every GPU vendor
misconceptions.correction: CUDA is proprietary/NVIDIA-specific; compatibility and alternative stacks exist for other vendors.
